title: Miracle flatness
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m_R)$ and $(S,\mathfrak m_S)$ be Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $\varphi:R\to S$ a local homomorphism ($\varphi(\mathfrak m_R)\subseteq\mathfrak m_S$). Assume (1) $R$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]; (2) $S$ is Cohen–Macaulay: $\operatorname{depth}(S)\ge\dim(S)$ [def-weil-pbc-depth], $\dim$ the Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] (that is, $\mathfrak m_S$ contains an $S$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] of length $\dim S$); (3) $\dim(S)=\dim(R)+\dim(S/\mathfrak m_RS)$, where $\mathfrak m_RS$ is the ideal of $S$ generated by $\varphi(\mathfrak m_R)$. Then $\varphi$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00R4 (lemma-CM-over-regular-flat, line 32654, slogan 'Miracle flatness')

proof.text: (The inductive claim.) For an integer $n\ge0$ let $P(n)$ be the assertion: for every local homomorphism $\varphi:R\to S$ of Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] satisfying (1), (2), (3) with $\dim R=n$, $\varphi$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. A regular local ring has finite dimension ($\mathfrak m_R$ is generated by $\dim R$ elements [def-weil-regular-scheme]), so the lemma is the conjunction of all $P(n)$, which we prove by induction on $n$: the base case $n=0$ is step 2, and steps 3–9 prove $P(n)$ for $n>0$ assuming $P(n-1)$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00R4 (lemma-CM-over-regular-flat, lines 32666-32690)

proof.text: (Base case $\dim R=0$.) By (1) [def-weil-regular-scheme] $\mathfrak m_R$ is generated by $\dim R=0$ elements, so $\mathfrak m_R=0$ and $R=R/\mathfrak m_R$ is a field. Every module over a field is flat [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat]; in particular $S$ is a flat $R$-module, i.e. $\varphi$ is flat.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00R4 (lemma-CM-over-regular-flat, lines 32666-32690)

proof.text: (Induction step: setup.) Let $n=\dim R>0$ and assume $P(n-1)$. Since $\varphi$ is local, $\mathfrak m_RS\subseteq\mathfrak m_S$, so $S/\mathfrak m_RS\ne0$ and $\dim(S/\mathfrak m_RS)\ge0$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]; by (3), $\dim S=\dim R+\dim(S/\mathfrak m_RS)\ge\dim R>0$ and $\dim(S/\mathfrak m_RS)=\dim S-\dim R<\dim S$ (all three dimensions are finite: $\dim S\le\dim_{\kappa_S}\mathfrak m_S/\mathfrak m_S^2<\infty$ for the Noetherian local ring $S$ by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension], and $\dim(S/\mathfrak m_RS)\le\dim S$ since primes of $S/\mathfrak m_RS$ are primes of $S$). By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-minimal-primes] $S$ has finitely many minimal prime ideals $\mathfrak q_1,\dots,\mathfrak q_r$ ($r\ge1$, since $S\ne0$ has a prime ideal and every prime contains a minimal one [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime]). Put $\mathfrak p_i=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q_i)$, a prime ideal of $R$; since $\mathfrak q_i\subseteq\mathfrak m_S$ and $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak m_S)=\mathfrak m_R$ ($\varphi$ is local and $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak m_S)$ is a proper ideal containing $\mathfrak m_R$), $\mathfrak p_i\subseteq\mathfrak m_R$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00R4 (lemma-CM-over-regular-flat, lines 32666-32690)

proof.text: ($\dim S/\mathfrak q_i=\dim S$.) Fix $i$. The prime ideals of $S/\mathfrak q_i$ are the $\mathfrak P/\mathfrak q_i$ with $\mathfrak P\supseteq\mathfrak q_i$ prime in $S$, inclusions preserved, so $e:=\dim(S/\mathfrak q_i)\le\dim S$ is finite [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]; choose a chain of primes $\mathfrak q_i=\mathfrak P_0\subsetneq\mathfrak P_1\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak P_e$ of $S$ of this maximal length $e$; it starts at $\mathfrak q_i$, since otherwise $\mathfrak q_i\subsetneq\mathfrak P_0$ could be prepended to give a longer chain of primes containing $\mathfrak q_i$. This chain is a maximal chain of prime ideals of $S$: no prime lies strictly below $\mathfrak P_0=\mathfrak q_i$ (minimality), and inserting a prime between two members or after $\mathfrak P_e$ would give a chain of primes containing $\mathfrak q_i$ of length $e+1$. Since $S$ is Cohen–Macaulay by (2), [lem-weil-pbc-cm-local-maximal-chain-length] gives $e=\dim S$. (Stacks: 'the first equality by Lemma 00N9'.)

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00R4 (lemma-CM-over-regular-flat, lines 32666-32690)

proof.text: ($\mathfrak p_i\neq\mathfrak m_R$.) Suppose $\mathfrak p_i=\mathfrak m_R$ for some $i$. Then $\varphi(\mathfrak m_R)\subseteq\mathfrak q_i$, so $\mathfrak m_RS\subseteq\mathfrak q_i$ and $S/\mathfrak q_i$ is a quotient of $S/\mathfrak m_RS$; a chain of primes of $S$ containing $\mathfrak q_i$ is a chain of primes containing $\mathfrak m_RS$, hence $\dim(S/\mathfrak q_i)\le\dim(S/\mathfrak m_RS)$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. With steps 3 and 4: $\dim S=\dim(S/\mathfrak q_i)\le\dim(S/\mathfrak m_RS)<\dim S$, a contradiction. Hence $\mathfrak p_i\subsetneq\mathfrak m_R$, i.e. $\mathfrak m_R\not\subseteq\mathfrak p_i$, for $i=1,\dots,r$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00R4 (lemma-CM-over-regular-flat, lines 32666-32690)

proof.text:
(Choice of $x$.) By (1) and [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension], $\dim_{\kappa}\mathfrak m_R/\mathfrak m_R^2=\dim R=n>0$ ($\kappa=R/\mathfrak m_R$), so $\mathfrak m_R
ot\subseteq\mathfrak m_R^2$. Apply prime avoidance [lem-weil-pbc-prime-avoidance] in $R$ to $J=\mathfrak m_R$ and the $r+1$ ideals $\mathfrak m_R^2,\mathfrak p_1,\dots,\mathfrak p_r$, all of which except $\mathfrak m_R^2$ are prime, none of which contains $J$ (step 5 and the above): there is $x\in\mathfrak m_R$ with $x
otin\mathfrak m_R^2$ and $x
otin\mathfrak p_i$ for all $i$. Then $\varphi(x)\in\mathfrak m_S$ and $\varphi(x)
otin\mathfrak q_i$ for all $i$ (as $\varphi(x)\in\mathfrak q_i$ would mean $x\in\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q_i)=\mathfrak p_i$): $\varphi(x)$ lies in no minimal prime of $S$. Write $xS$ for $\varphi(x)S$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00R4 (lemma-CM-over-regular-flat, lines 32666-32690)

proof.text: ($R/xR$ is regular of dimension $n-1$, and $x$ is a nonzerodivisor on $R$.) Since $x\notin\mathfrak m_R^2$, its class $\bar x$ in the $n$-dimensional $\kappa$-vector space $\mathfrak m_R/\mathfrak m_R^2$ [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension] is nonzero and extends to a basis $\bar x,\bar y_2,\dots,\bar y_n$; with lifts $y_j\in\mathfrak m_R$, the elements $x_1=x,x_2=y_2,\dots,x_n=y_n$ generate the finitely generated $R$-module $\mathfrak m_R$ by Nakayama's lemma [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] (their images span $\mathfrak m_R/\mathfrak m_R\cdot\mathfrak m_R$). These are $n=\dim R$ generators of $\mathfrak m_R$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] $x_1,\dots,x_n$ is a regular sequence in $R$ — in particular $x$ is a nonzerodivisor on $R$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] — and (with $c=1$) $R/xR$ is a regular local ring of dimension $n-1$. (Stacks: 'By (1) and Lemma 00NQ the ring R/xR is regular with dim(R/xR) = dim(R) - 1'.)

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00R4 (lemma-CM-over-regular-flat, lines 32666-32690)

proof.text: ($x$ is a nonzerodivisor on $S$, and $S/xS$ is Cohen–Macaulay of dimension $\dim S-1$.) Since $\varphi(x)\in\mathfrak m_S$ lies in no minimal prime of $S$ (step 6), [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-dim-drop-outside-minimal-primes] gives $\dim(S/xS)=\dim S-1$. Since $S$ is Cohen–Macaulay by (2), [lem-weil-pbc-cm-local-dimension-drop-regular-sequence] with $c=1$, $g_1=\varphi(x)$ shows that $\varphi(x)$ is a regular sequence of length one in $S$, i.e. multiplication by $\varphi(x)$ on $S$ is injective [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Then [lem-weil-pbc-cm-local-quotient-nonzerodivisor-cm] shows that $S/xS$ is a Noetherian local ring with $\operatorname{depth}(S/xS)\ge\dim(S/xS)=\dim S-1$ [def-weil-pbc-depth]. (Stacks: 'x is a nonzerodivisor on S by (2), see Lemma 02JN, and S/xS is Cohen–Macaulay with dim(S/xS) = dim(S) - 1'.)

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00R4 (lemma-CM-over-regular-flat, lines 32666-32690)

proof.text: (The hypotheses descend to $R/xR\to S/xS$.) Put $\bar R=R/xR$, $\bar S=S/xS$. As $\varphi(xR)\subseteq xS$, $\varphi$ induces a ring map $\bar\varphi:\bar R\to\bar S$; both are Noetherian local rings (quotients of Noetherian local rings by ideals inside the maximal ideals) with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_{\bar R}=\mathfrak m_R/xR$ and $\mathfrak m_{\bar S}=\mathfrak m_S/xS$, and $\bar\varphi(\mathfrak m_{\bar R})\subseteq\mathfrak m_{\bar S}$, so $\bar\varphi$ is local. Hypothesis (1) for $\bar R$ is step 7 ($\bar R$ regular, $\dim\bar R=n-1$); (2) for $\bar S$ is step 8. For (3): the ideal $\mathfrak m_{\bar R}\bar S$ is the image of $\mathfrak m_RS$ in $\bar S$, and $xS\subseteq\mathfrak m_RS$ because $x\in\mathfrak m_R$; hence $\bar S/\mathfrak m_{\bar R}\bar S\cong S/\mathfrak m_RS$, and with steps 7 and 8, $\dim\bar S=\dim S-1=(\dim R-1)+\dim(S/\mathfrak m_RS)=\dim\bar R+\dim(\bar S/\mathfrak m_{\bar R}\bar S)$. By the induction hypothesis $P(n-1)$, $\bar\varphi:R/xR\to S/xS$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00R4 (lemma-CM-over-regular-flat, lines 32666-32690)

proof.text: (Local criterion of flatness.) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-criterion-nonzerodivisor] to the local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings $\varphi:R\to S$, the finitely generated $S$-module $M=S$ (generated by $1$) [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and $x\in\mathfrak m_R$: $x$ is a nonzerodivisor on $R$ (step 7), multiplication by $\varphi(x)$ on $M=S$ is injective (step 8), and $M/xM=S/xS$ is flat over $R/xR$ (step 9; the $R/xR$-module structure of $S/xS$ is the one through $\bar\varphi$). Hence $S$ is a flat $R$-module, i.e. $\varphi$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. This proves $P(n)$ and completes the induction. (Stacks: 'we conclude by Lemma 00ML and the remark following it'.)
